'**Phantasm** / When Dunebreaker Cenipai is destroyed, create an Ash token. / **Go again**' Draconic Illusionist Action - Attack.

PRINTED KEYWORDS NOT AUTHORED: GoAgain and Phantasm are both in printed_keywords and fire from the card DB keywords field (Phantasm via ability_keywords.phantasm_check/phantasm_destroy, CR 8.3.13); re-authoring either would be a defect.

SHAPE copied from the SHIPPED upr/embermaw_cenipai_yellow.json - same Cenipai family, same 'When <Cenipai> is destroyed, create an Ash token' text, whose spelling provably compiles: TRIGGERED ON_DEATH + CREATE_TOKEN token_type 'Ash'. The handler reads token/token_name/token_type/token_slug interchangeably (effect_types.py:1947-1948) and create_token slugifies the display name to 'ash'; json/tokens/ash.json exists, so resolution will not raise MissingCardImplementation.

KNOWN DEVIATION FROM RELEASE NOTE 1, disclosed: the note restricts the trigger to destruction WHILE IN THE ARENA - not as a defending card, not on the stack, not in arsenal. ON_DEATH is dispatched by engine._dsl_destroyed_listener (engine.py:1578-1588) for EVERY canonical destroy(), including phantasm_destroy's destruction of a DEFENDING card (ability_keywords.py:412-415 routes through _ek_destroy) - precisely the case the note excludes - and equally for a destruction while on the stack or in arsenal. Not expressible: no DSL condition reads the destroyed card's ORIGIN zone. The DestroyEvent payload carries target/destroy_source/source_player_id/canceled only (effect_keywords.py:688-693), and by condition-evaluation time the card sits in the graveyard on every path, so zone-testing conditions cannot separate the cases. destroy() even computes 'was_arena' internally (effect_keywords.py:705) but does not expose it to the DSL. Drafted bare to match the shipped sibling; if the destroy event ever exposes was_arena, gate this ability on it.

Normal resolution of the attack sends the card to the graveyard WITHOUT destroying it, so the common post-combat path does not fire this - only actual destroy() effects do.
